Lab 12. Q-Learning on FrozenLake¶

In this lab, you will get hands-on experience with reinforcement learning using tabular Q-learning.

Specifically, we will go through the following steps:

  • Create a FrozenLake grid-world environment with Gymnasium.
  • Interpret FrozenLake as a Markov Decision Process.
  • Train a tabular Q-learning agent.
  • Visualize the learned Q-table and greedy policy.
  • Animate how the policy changes during training.
  • Evaluate the learned policy on held-out episodes.
  • Run tinker experiments with learning rate, discount factor, exploration, and reward shaping.

You do not need to build a full RL system from scratch. The key Q-learning update is included, and your job is to run, inspect, and change settings to see how learning behavior changes.

Step 0. Setup¶

This notebook uses Gymnasium's modern API:

state, info = env.reset()
next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
done = terminated or truncated

The notebook should already work in the course environment. If gymnasium or imageio is missing locally, the setup cell will try to install it.

Step 1. Create the FrozenLake Environment¶

FrozenLake is a small grid-world environment.

The agent starts at S, tries to reach the goal G, and should avoid holes H. Safe frozen tiles are marked F.

Note: Choose a Demo Mode¶

For teaching, it helps to have two modes:

  • perfect_demo: deterministic FrozenLake with is_slippery=False, so the learned policy is crisp and easy to interpret
  • stochastic_discussion: slippery FrozenLake with is_slippery=True, so students can discuss exploration, stochastic transitions, and noisier policies

Use perfect_demo for the main homework/demo run.

Step 2. FrozenLake as an MDP¶

A Markov Decision Process, or MDP, has states, actions, transition dynamics, and rewards.

In FrozenLake:

  • states are grid positions
  • actions are left, down, right, and up
  • transitions move the agent around the grid
  • rewards tell the agent whether it reached the goal

The cell below prints the map and action meanings.

In [4]:
# Action meanings used by FrozenLake:
# 0 = left, 1 = down, 2 = right, 3 = up

ACTION_NAMES = ["Left", "Down", "Right", "Up"]
ACTION_ARROWS = np.array(["←", "↓", "→", "↑"])

def make_frozenlake(map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, render_mode="ansi"):
    """Create a FrozenLake environment with consistent defaults."""
    return gym.make(
        "FrozenLake-v1",
        map_name=map_name,
        is_slippery=is_slippery,
        render_mode=render_mode
    )

def decode_grid(env):
    """Return the FrozenLake map as a 2D array of strings."""
    desc = env.unwrapped.desc
    return np.array([
        [cell.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(cell, bytes) else str(cell) for cell in row]
        for row in desc
    ])

def state_to_row_col(state, env):
    """Convert a one-number state index into a grid row and column."""
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_cols = grid.shape[1]
    return divmod(int(state), n_cols)

def tile_for_state(env, state):
    """Return S, F, H, or G for a given state."""
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    row, col = state_to_row_col(state, env)
    return grid[row, col]

# Inspect the map and state/action counts.
env = make_frozenlake()
grid = decode_grid(env)

print("Map:")
for row in grid:
    print(" ".join(row))

print()
print("Number of states:", env.observation_space.n)
print("Number of actions:", env.action_space.n)
print("Actions:", dict(enumerate(ACTION_NAMES)))

env.close()

def greedy_action(Q, state, rng):
    """Break ties randomly among actions with the same max Q-value."""
    row = Q[state]
    max_q = np.max(row)
    best_actions = np.flatnonzero(np.isclose(row, max_q))
    return int(rng.choice(best_actions))

Step 3. Helper Functions for Plotting and Watching Behavior¶

The helper functions below make the Q-table and learned policy easier to inspect.

They let us:

  • plot state-action Q-values
  • plot the greedy action for each grid cell
  • print policies and trajectories
  • plot training success over time
  • animate trajectories

You do not need to memorize every helper. Focus on the visual outputs they produce.

In [5]:
def plot_q_table(Q, title="Q-table heatmap"):
    """Plot the Q-table as states x actions."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
    image = ax.imshow(Q, aspect="auto")
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel("Action")
    ax.set_ylabel("State")
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(Q.shape[1]), ACTION_NAMES)
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(Q.shape[0]))

    for state in range(Q.shape[0]):
        for action in range(Q.shape[1]):
            ax.text(action, state, f"{Q[state, action]:.2f}",
                    ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8)

    cbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax)
    cbar.set_label("Q-value")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def plot_policy(Q, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, title="Greedy policy from Q-table"):
    """Plot max Q-value by state, with greedy action arrows over the grid."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_rows, n_cols = grid.shape

    values = np.max(Q, axis=1).reshape(n_rows, n_cols)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 5))
    image = ax.imshow(values)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(n_cols))
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_rows))

    for state in range(Q.shape[0]):
        row, col = divmod(state, n_cols)
        tile = grid[row, col]

        if tile == "H":
            label = "H"
        elif tile == "G":
            label = "G"
        else:
            label = ACTION_ARROWS[int(np.argmax(Q[state]))]

        ax.text(col, row, label, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=18)

    cbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax)
    cbar.set_label("max Q-value")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    env.close()


def moving_average(values, window):
    """Simple moving average for smoothing training curves."""
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    if len(values) < window:
        return values
    weights = np.ones(window) / window
    return np.convolve(values, weights, mode="valid")


def plot_training(history, window=100, title="Training success rate"):
    """Plot moving average of success over training episodes."""
    success = np.asarray(history["success"], dtype=float)
    smoothed = moving_average(success, window)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))

    if len(success) >= window:
        x = np.arange(window - 1, window - 1 + len(smoothed))
        ax.plot(x, smoothed)
        ax.set_ylabel(f"Success rate, {window}-episode moving average")
    else:
        ax.plot(success)
        ax.set_ylabel("Success: 1 = reached goal, 0 = did not")

    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel("Episode")
    ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.05)
    ax.grid(True)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def print_policy(Q, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY):
    """Print a text version of the greedy policy."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_rows, n_cols = grid.shape

    print("Greedy policy:")
    for row in range(n_rows):
        labels = []
        for col in range(n_cols):
            state = row * n_cols + col
            tile = grid[row, col]

            if tile in ["H", "G"]:
                labels.append(tile)
            else:
                labels.append(ACTION_ARROWS[int(np.argmax(Q[state]))])
        print(" ".join(labels))
    env.close()


def print_trajectory(states, actions, rewards, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY):
    """Print a compact trajectory summary."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_cols = grid.shape[1]

    print("States:")
    print(" -> ".join(str(s) for s in states))

    if actions:
        print("Actions:")
        print(" -> ".join(ACTION_NAMES[a] for a in actions))

    print("Rewards:")
    print(rewards)

    final_state = states[-1]
    final_tile = tile_for_state(env, final_state)
    print("Final tile:", final_tile)

    path_grid = grid.copy()
    for state in states[:-1]:
        row, col = divmod(state, n_cols)
        if path_grid[row, col] == "F":
            path_grid[row, col] = "·"

    row, col = divmod(final_state, n_cols)
    if path_grid[row, col] not in ["H", "G"]:
        path_grid[row, col] = "A"

    print()
    print("Path grid:")
    for row in path_grid:
        print(" ".join(row))

    env.close()


def animate_trajectory(states, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, pause=0.35):
    """Animate a saved trajectory in text form."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_cols = grid.shape[1]

    for step, state in enumerate(states):
        clear_output(wait=True)
        frame = grid.copy()
        row, col = divmod(state, n_cols)
        frame[row, col] = "A"

        print(f"Step {step} of {len(states) - 1}")
        for grid_row in frame:
            print(" ".join(grid_row))
        sleep(pause)

    env.close()

Step 4. Reward Shaping Helper¶

Reward shaping changes the reward signal used during learning.

The default FrozenLake reward gives a reward for reaching the goal. The custom reward mode can also add a step penalty, hole penalty, or larger goal reward.

Changing rewards can make learning easier or harder, but it can also change what behavior the agent is encouraged to learn.

In [6]:
def apply_reward_mode(
    env,
    next_state,
    original_reward,
    reward_mode="default",
    step_penalty=0.0,
    hole_penalty=0.0,
    goal_reward=1.0
):
    """
    Return the reward used for learning.

    reward_mode="default":
        Use FrozenLake's original reward.

    reward_mode="custom":
        Use a simple custom reward:
        - every step gets step_penalty
        - landing in a hole adds hole_penalty
        - landing on the goal adds goal_reward
    """
    if reward_mode == "default":
        return original_reward

    if reward_mode != "custom":
        raise ValueError("reward_mode must be either 'default' or 'custom'.")

    tile = tile_for_state(env, next_state)
    shaped_reward = step_penalty

    if tile == "H":
        shaped_reward += hole_penalty
    elif tile == "G":
        shaped_reward += goal_reward

    return shaped_reward

Step 5. Q-Learning Training Loop¶

Q-learning learns a table Q[state, action].

Each value estimates how good it is to take a particular action from a particular state.

The training loop uses epsilon-greedy action selection:

  • with probability epsilon, explore with a random action
  • otherwise, exploit the best action according to the current Q-table

The update rule combines the reward now with the best estimated future value.

In [7]:
def train_q_learning(
    episodes=3000,
    max_steps_per_episode=100,
    alpha=0.30,
    gamma=0.95,
    epsilon_start=1.00,
    epsilon_end=0.05,
    epsilon_decay=0.995,
    map_name=MAP_NAME,
    is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY,
    seed=SEED,
    reward_mode="default",
    step_penalty=0.0,
    hole_penalty=0.0,
    goal_reward=1.0
):
    """
    Train a tabular Q-learning agent on FrozenLake.

    Returns:
        Q: learned Q-table, shape [num_states, num_actions]
        history: dictionary with training statistics
    """
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    n_states = env.observation_space.n
    n_actions = env.action_space.n

    Q = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    successes = []
    episode_returns = []
    episode_lengths = []
    epsilons = []

    epsilon = epsilon_start

    for episode in range(episodes):
        state, info = env.reset(seed=seed + episode)
        original_return = 0.0
        reached_goal = False

        for step in range(max_steps_per_episode):
            # Epsilon-greedy action selection:
            # Explore with probability epsilon, otherwise exploit the best known action.
            if rng.random() < epsilon:
                action = int(rng.integers(n_actions))
            else:
                action = greedy_action(Q, state, rng)

            next_state, original_reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
            done = terminated or truncated

            learning_reward = apply_reward_mode(
                env,
                next_state,
                original_reward,
                reward_mode=reward_mode,
                step_penalty=step_penalty,
                hole_penalty=hole_penalty,
                goal_reward=goal_reward
            )

            # ---------- STUDENT FOCUS: Q-learning update rule ----------
            best_next_q = np.max(Q[next_state])
            bootstrap = 0.0 if terminated else best_next_q
            td_target = learning_reward + gamma * bootstrap
            td_error = td_target - Q[state, action]
            Q[state, action] = Q[state, action] + alpha * td_error
            # ---------------------------------------------------------

            original_return += original_reward

            if original_reward > 0:
                reached_goal = True

            state = next_state

            if done:
                break

        successes.append(reached_goal)
        episode_returns.append(original_return)
        episode_lengths.append(step + 1)
        epsilons.append(epsilon)

        epsilon = max(epsilon_end, epsilon * epsilon_decay)

    env.close()

    history = {
        "success": np.array(successes, dtype=bool),
        "episode_return": np.array(episode_returns, dtype=float),
        "episode_length": np.array(episode_lengths, dtype=int),
        "epsilon": np.array(epsilons, dtype=float),
        "params": {
            "episodes": episodes,
            "max_steps_per_episode": max_steps_per_episode,
            "alpha": alpha,
            "gamma": gamma,
            "epsilon_start": epsilon_start,
            "epsilon_end": epsilon_end,
            "epsilon_decay": epsilon_decay,
            "map_name": map_name,
            "is_slippery": is_slippery,
            "seed": seed,
            "reward_mode": reward_mode,
            "step_penalty": step_penalty,
            "hole_penalty": hole_penalty,
            "goal_reward": goal_reward
        }
    }

    return Q, history

Note: Reading the Policy Plot¶

  • H means hole, a terminal failure state.
  • G means goal, a terminal success state.
  • Arrows show the action with the highest Q-value in each non-terminal state.
  • Brighter squares mean larger maximum Q-values.

Use this plot to see whether the learned policy moves around holes and toward the goal.

Step 7. Animate the Learned Policy During Training¶

Sometimes a single final policy plot hides the learning process.

The next cells create an updating GIF that shows how the policy and state values change as training progresses.

Suggested uses:

  • keep the default settings and watch the policy become more organized
  • compare deterministic vs. slippery FrozenLake
  • change the snapshot interval to make the GIF shorter or smoother
In [10]:
def policy_frame_array(Q, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, title="Policy snapshot"):
    """Render a policy plot to an RGB image array so it can be written into a GIF."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_rows, n_cols = grid.shape

    values = np.max(Q, axis=1).reshape(n_rows, n_cols)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 5))
    image = ax.imshow(values)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(n_cols))
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_rows))

    for state in range(Q.shape[0]):
        row, col = divmod(state, n_cols)
        tile = grid[row, col]

        if tile == "H":
            label = "H"
        elif tile == "G":
            label = "G"
        else:
            # Random tie-breaking is useful during training, but for a stable figure
            # we show the greedy action from np.argmax here.
            label = ACTION_ARROWS[int(np.argmax(Q[state]))]

        ax.text(col, row, label, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=18)

    cbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax)
    cbar.set_label("max Q-value")
    plt.tight_layout()

    fig.canvas.draw()
    width, height = fig.canvas.get_width_height()
    frame = np.frombuffer(fig.canvas.buffer_rgba(), dtype=np.uint8).reshape(height, width, 4)[..., :3].copy()
    plt.close(fig)
    env.close()
    return frame


def train_q_learning_with_snapshots(
    episodes=3000,
    max_steps_per_episode=100,
    alpha=0.30,
    gamma=0.95,
    epsilon_start=1.00,
    epsilon_end=0.05,
    epsilon_decay=0.995,
    map_name=MAP_NAME,
    is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY,
    seed=SEED,
    reward_mode="default",
    step_penalty=0.0,
    hole_penalty=0.0,
    goal_reward=1.0,
    snapshot_interval=250
):
    """Train Q-learning and save policy snapshots every snapshot_interval episodes."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    n_states = env.observation_space.n
    n_actions = env.action_space.n

    Q = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    successes = []
    episode_returns = []
    episode_lengths = []
    epsilons = []

    snapshots = []
    epsilon = epsilon_start

    # Initial frame before training
    snapshots.append({
        "episode": 0,
        "Q": Q.copy()
    })

    for episode in range(episodes):
        state, info = env.reset(seed=seed + episode)
        original_return = 0.0
        reached_goal = False

        for step in range(max_steps_per_episode):
            if rng.random() < epsilon:
                action = int(rng.integers(n_actions))
            else:
                action = greedy_action(Q, state, rng)

            next_state, original_reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
            done = terminated or truncated

            learning_reward = apply_reward_mode(
                env,
                next_state,
                original_reward,
                reward_mode=reward_mode,
                step_penalty=step_penalty,
                hole_penalty=hole_penalty,
                goal_reward=goal_reward
            )

            best_next_q = np.max(Q[next_state])
            bootstrap = 0.0 if terminated else best_next_q
            td_target = learning_reward + gamma * bootstrap
            td_error = td_target - Q[state, action]
            Q[state, action] = Q[state, action] + alpha * td_error

            original_return += original_reward
            if original_reward > 0:
                reached_goal = True

            state = next_state
            if done:
                break

        successes.append(reached_goal)
        episode_returns.append(original_return)
        episode_lengths.append(step + 1)
        epsilons.append(epsilon)

        completed_episode = episode + 1
        if completed_episode % snapshot_interval == 0:
            snapshots.append({
                "episode": completed_episode,
                "Q": Q.copy()
            })

        epsilon = max(epsilon_end, epsilon * epsilon_decay)

    # Always include the final trained policy
    if snapshots[-1]["episode"] != episodes:
        snapshots.append({
            "episode": episodes,
            "Q": Q.copy()
        })

    env.close()

    history = {
        "success": np.array(successes, dtype=bool),
        "episode_return": np.array(episode_returns, dtype=float),
        "episode_length": np.array(episode_lengths, dtype=int),
        "epsilon": np.array(epsilons, dtype=float),
        "params": {
            "episodes": episodes,
            "max_steps_per_episode": max_steps_per_episode,
            "alpha": alpha,
            "gamma": gamma,
            "epsilon_start": epsilon_start,
            "epsilon_end": epsilon_end,
            "epsilon_decay": epsilon_decay,
            "map_name": map_name,
            "is_slippery": is_slippery,
            "seed": seed,
            "reward_mode": reward_mode,
            "step_penalty": step_penalty,
            "hole_penalty": hole_penalty,
            "goal_reward": goal_reward,
            "snapshot_interval": snapshot_interval
        }
    }

    return Q, history, snapshots


def save_policy_gif(snapshots, out_path, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, fps=2):
    """Convert saved Q-table snapshots into an animated GIF."""
    frames = []
    for snap in snapshots:
        title = f"Learned policy after episode {snap['episode']}"
        frame = policy_frame_array(
            snap["Q"],
            map_name=map_name,
            is_slippery=is_slippery,
            title=title
        )
        frames.append(frame)

    imageio.mimsave(out_path, frames, fps=fps, loop=0)
    return out_path

Step 8. Evaluate the Learned Greedy Policy¶

Now evaluate the fixed Q-table over multiple episodes.

During evaluation, the agent usually acts greedily, meaning it chooses the best action according to the learned Q-table instead of exploring.

The evaluation reports success rate, average return, and average episode length.

In [13]:
def evaluate_agent(
    Q,
    episodes=100,
    max_steps_per_episode=100,
    epsilon=0.0,
    map_name=MAP_NAME,
    is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY,
    seed=10_000
):
    """Evaluate a fixed Q-table."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n_actions = env.action_space.n

    successes = []
    returns = []
    lengths = []

    for episode in range(episodes):
        state, info = env.reset(seed=seed + episode)
        total_reward = 0.0
        reached_goal = False

        for step in range(max_steps_per_episode):
            if rng.random() < epsilon:
                action = int(rng.integers(n_actions))
            else:
                action = greedy_action(Q, state, rng)

            next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
            done = terminated or truncated

            total_reward += reward
            if reward > 0:
                reached_goal = True

            state = next_state

            if done:
                break

        successes.append(reached_goal)
        returns.append(total_reward)
        lengths.append(step + 1)

    env.close()

    return {
        "success_rate": float(np.mean(successes)),
        "average_return": float(np.mean(returns)),
        "average_length": float(np.mean(lengths))
    }


evaluation = evaluate_agent(
    Q,
    episodes=100,
    map_name=MAP_NAME,
    is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY
)

print("Greedy policy evaluation:")
for key, value in evaluation.items():
    print(f"  {key}: {value:.3f}")

Step 9. Watch the Trajectory Improve¶

This section compares behavior before and after training.

First, collect a trajectory from an untrained all-zero Q-table. Then collect a trajectory from the trained Q-table.

The printed and animated trajectories should make the effect of learning visible.

In [14]:
def collect_trajectory(
    Q,
    max_steps=25,
    epsilon=0.0,
    map_name=MAP_NAME,
    is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY,
    seed=1234
):
    """Collect one trajectory from a fixed Q-table."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n_actions = env.action_space.n

    state, info = env.reset(seed=seed)
    states = [int(state)]
    actions = []
    rewards = []

    for step in range(max_steps):
        if rng.random() < epsilon:
            action = int(rng.integers(n_actions))
        else:
            action = greedy_action(Q, state, rng)

        next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)

        actions.append(action)
        rewards.append(float(reward))
        states.append(int(next_state))

        state = next_state

        if terminated or truncated:
            break

    env.close()
    return states, actions, rewards

Step 10. Tinker Experiment Runner¶

The helper below runs one experiment using the baseline settings plus whichever overrides you provide.

Each experiment trains a new Q-table, prints the changed settings, plots the training curve, and plots the learned policy.

In [19]:
def run_tinker_experiment(label, **overrides):
    """Run one experiment using baseline settings plus selected overrides."""
    params = BASELINE_PARAMS.copy()
    params.update(overrides)

    Q_exp, history_exp = train_q_learning(**params)

    final_window = min(100, len(history_exp["success"]))
    final_success_rate = history_exp["success"][-final_window:].mean()

    print("=" * 70)
    print(label)
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Final {final_window}-episode success rate: {final_success_rate:.1%}")
    print("Changed settings:")
    for key, value in overrides.items():
        print(f"  {key}: {value}")

    plot_training(history_exp, window=100, title=f"{label}: training success rate")
    plot_policy(Q_exp, map_name=params["map_name"], is_slippery=params["is_slippery"],
                title=f"{label}: learned policy")

    return Q_exp, history_exp

Step 11. Group A: Learning Rate Experiment¶

The learning rate alpha controls how much each new update changes the Q-table.

Turn this group on to compare small, medium, and large learning rates. Watch for settings that learn too slowly or update too aggressively.

Lab 12. Q-Learning on FrozenLake¶

Student version: This copy keeps the setup and helper code in place, but removes a small number of essential solution pieces. Each marked cell has comments and hints showing exactly what to complete.

In this lab, you will get hands-on experience with reinforcement learning using tabular Q-learning.

Specifically, we will go through the following steps:

  • Create a FrozenLake grid-world environment with Gymnasium.
  • Interpret FrozenLake as a Markov Decision Process.
  • Train a tabular Q-learning agent.
  • Visualize the learned Q-table and greedy policy.
  • Animate how the policy changes during training.
  • Evaluate the learned policy on held-out episodes.
  • Run tinker experiments with learning rate, discount factor, exploration, and reward shaping.

You do not need to build a full RL system from scratch. The key Q-learning update is included, and your job is to run, inspect, and change settings to see how learning behavior changes.

Step 0. Setup¶

This notebook uses Gymnasium's modern API:

state, info = env.reset()
next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
done = terminated or truncated

Step 1. Create the FrozenLake Environment¶

FrozenLake is a small grid-world environment.

The agent starts at S, tries to reach the goal G, and should avoid holes H. Safe frozen tiles are marked F.

Note: Choose a Demo Mode¶

For teaching, it helps to have two modes:

  • perfect_demo: deterministic FrozenLake with is_slippery=False, so the learned policy is crisp and easy to interpret
  • stochastic_discussion: slippery FrozenLake with is_slippery=True, so students can discuss exploration, stochastic transitions, and noisier policies

Use perfect_demo for the main homework/demo run.

Step 2. FrozenLake as an MDP¶

A Markov Decision Process, or MDP, has states, actions, transition dynamics, and rewards.

In FrozenLake:

  • states are grid positions
  • actions are left, down, right, and up
  • transitions move the agent around the grid
  • rewards tell the agent whether it reached the goal

The cell below prints the map and action meanings.

In [ ]:
# Action meanings used by FrozenLake:
# 0 = left, 1 = down, 2 = right, 3 = up

ACTION_NAMES = ["Left", "Down", "Right", "Up"]
ACTION_ARROWS = np.array(["←", "↓", "→", "↑"])

def make_frozenlake(map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, render_mode="ansi"):
    """Create a FrozenLake environment with consistent defaults."""
    return gym.make(
        "FrozenLake-v1",
        map_name=map_name,
        is_slippery=is_slippery,
        render_mode=render_mode
    )

def decode_grid(env):
    """Return the FrozenLake map as a 2D array of strings."""
    desc = env.unwrapped.desc
    return np.array([
        [cell.decode("utf-8") if isinstance(cell, bytes) else str(cell) for cell in row]
        for row in desc
    ])

def state_to_row_col(state, env):
    """Convert a one-number state index into a grid row and column."""
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_cols = grid.shape[1]
    return divmod(int(state), n_cols)

def tile_for_state(env, state):
    """Return S, F, H, or G for a given state."""
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    row, col = state_to_row_col(state, env)
    return grid[row, col]

# Inspect the map and state/action counts.
env = make_frozenlake()
grid = decode_grid(env)

print("Map:")
for row in grid:
    print(" ".join(row))

print()
print("Number of states:", env.observation_space.n)
print("Number of actions:", env.action_space.n)
print("Actions:", dict(enumerate(ACTION_NAMES)))

env.close()

def greedy_action(Q, state, rng):
    """Break ties randomly among actions with the same max Q-value."""
    row = Q[state]
    max_q = np.max(row)
    best_actions = np.flatnonzero(np.isclose(row, max_q))
    return int(rng.choice(best_actions))

Step 3. Helper Functions for Plotting and Watching Behavior¶

The helper functions below make the Q-table and learned policy easier to inspect.

They let us:

  • plot state-action Q-values
  • plot the greedy action for each grid cell
  • print policies and trajectories
  • plot training success over time
  • animate trajectories

You do not need to memorize every helper. Focus on the visual outputs they produce.

In [ ]:
def plot_q_table(Q, title="Q-table heatmap"):
    """Plot the Q-table as states x actions."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
    image = ax.imshow(Q, aspect="auto")
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel("Action")
    ax.set_ylabel("State")
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(Q.shape[1]), ACTION_NAMES)
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(Q.shape[0]))

    for state in range(Q.shape[0]):
        for action in range(Q.shape[1]):
            ax.text(action, state, f"{Q[state, action]:.2f}",
                    ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8)

    cbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax)
    cbar.set_label("Q-value")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def plot_policy(Q, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, title="Greedy policy from Q-table"):
    """Plot max Q-value by state, with greedy action arrows over the grid."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_rows, n_cols = grid.shape

    values = np.max(Q, axis=1).reshape(n_rows, n_cols)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 5))
    image = ax.imshow(values)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(n_cols))
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_rows))

    for state in range(Q.shape[0]):
        row, col = divmod(state, n_cols)
        tile = grid[row, col]

        if tile == "H":
            label = "H"
        elif tile == "G":
            label = "G"
        else:
            label = ACTION_ARROWS[int(np.argmax(Q[state]))]

        ax.text(col, row, label, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=18)

    cbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax)
    cbar.set_label("max Q-value")
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    env.close()


def moving_average(values, window):
    """Simple moving average for smoothing training curves."""
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    if len(values) < window:
        return values
    weights = np.ones(window) / window
    return np.convolve(values, weights, mode="valid")


def plot_training(history, window=100, title="Training success rate"):
    """Plot moving average of success over training episodes."""
    success = np.asarray(history["success"], dtype=float)
    smoothed = moving_average(success, window)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))

    if len(success) >= window:
        x = np.arange(window - 1, window - 1 + len(smoothed))
        ax.plot(x, smoothed)
        ax.set_ylabel(f"Success rate, {window}-episode moving average")
    else:
        ax.plot(success)
        ax.set_ylabel("Success: 1 = reached goal, 0 = did not")

    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xlabel("Episode")
    ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.05)
    ax.grid(True)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()


def print_policy(Q, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY):
    """Print a text version of the greedy policy."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_rows, n_cols = grid.shape

    print("Greedy policy:")
    for row in range(n_rows):
        labels = []
        for col in range(n_cols):
            state = row * n_cols + col
            tile = grid[row, col]

            if tile in ["H", "G"]:
                labels.append(tile)
            else:
                labels.append(ACTION_ARROWS[int(np.argmax(Q[state]))])
        print(" ".join(labels))
    env.close()


def print_trajectory(states, actions, rewards, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY):
    """Print a compact trajectory summary."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_cols = grid.shape[1]

    print("States:")
    print(" -> ".join(str(s) for s in states))

    if actions:
        print("Actions:")
        print(" -> ".join(ACTION_NAMES[a] for a in actions))

    print("Rewards:")
    print(rewards)

    final_state = states[-1]
    final_tile = tile_for_state(env, final_state)
    print("Final tile:", final_tile)

    path_grid = grid.copy()
    for state in states[:-1]:
        row, col = divmod(state, n_cols)
        if path_grid[row, col] == "F":
            path_grid[row, col] = "·"

    row, col = divmod(final_state, n_cols)
    if path_grid[row, col] not in ["H", "G"]:
        path_grid[row, col] = "A"

    print()
    print("Path grid:")
    for row in path_grid:
        print(" ".join(row))

    env.close()


def animate_trajectory(states, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, pause=0.35):
    """Animate a saved trajectory in text form."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_cols = grid.shape[1]

    for step, state in enumerate(states):
        clear_output(wait=True)
        frame = grid.copy()
        row, col = divmod(state, n_cols)
        frame[row, col] = "A"

        print(f"Step {step} of {len(states) - 1}")
        for grid_row in frame:
            print(" ".join(grid_row))
        sleep(pause)

    env.close()

Step 4. Reward Shaping Helper¶

Reward shaping changes the reward signal used during learning.

The default FrozenLake reward gives a reward for reaching the goal. The custom reward mode can also add a step penalty, hole penalty, or larger goal reward.

Changing rewards can make learning easier or harder, but it can also change what behavior the agent is encouraged to learn.

#   2. start shaped_reward at step_penalty

        ...
    elif tile == "G":

Step 5. Q-Learning Training Loop¶

Q-learning learns a table Q[state, action].

Each value estimates how good it is to take a particular action from a particular state.

The training loop uses epsilon-greedy action selection:

  • with probability epsilon, explore with a random action
  • otherwise, exploit the best action according to the current Q-table

The update rule combines the reward now with the best estimated future value.

In [ ]:
# TODO 2: Complete epsilon-greedy action selection and the Q-learning update.
#
# Everything around the update is provided. Fill the focused lines marked with
# ellipses.
#
# Epsilon-greedy action selection:
#   rng.random() gives a random number in [0, 1).
#   rng.integers(n_actions) samples a random action id.
#   greedy_action(Q, state, rng) returns the best known action.
#
# Q-learning update:
#   best_next_q = max_a Q[next_state, a]
#   bootstrap = 0 if terminated else best_next_q
#   td_target = learning_reward + gamma * bootstrap
#   td_error = td_target - Q[state, action]
#   Q[state, action] += alpha * td_error

def train_q_learning(
    episodes=3000,
    max_steps_per_episode=100,
    alpha=0.30,
    gamma=0.95,
    epsilon_start=1.00,
    epsilon_end=0.05,
    epsilon_decay=0.995,
    map_name=MAP_NAME,
    is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY,
    seed=SEED,
    reward_mode="default",
    step_penalty=0.0,
    hole_penalty=0.0,
    goal_reward=1.0
):
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    n_states = env.observation_space.n
    n_actions = env.action_space.n

    Q = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    successes = []
    episode_returns = []
    episode_lengths = []
    epsilons = []
    epsilon = epsilon_start

    for episode in range(episodes):
        state, info = env.reset(seed=seed + episode)
        original_return = 0.0
        reached_goal = False

        for step in range(max_steps_per_episode):
            if rng.random() < epsilon:
                action = ...
            else:
                action = ...

            next_state, original_reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
            done = terminated or truncated

            learning_reward = apply_reward_mode(
                env,
                next_state,
                original_reward,
                reward_mode=reward_mode,
                step_penalty=step_penalty,
                hole_penalty=hole_penalty,
                goal_reward=goal_reward
            )

            best_next_q = ...
            bootstrap = ...
            td_target = ...
            td_error = ...
            Q[state, action] = ...

            original_return += original_reward
            if original_reward > 0:
                reached_goal = True
            state = next_state
            if done:
                break

        successes.append(reached_goal)
        episode_returns.append(original_return)
        episode_lengths.append(step + 1)
        epsilons.append(epsilon)
        epsilon = max(epsilon_end, epsilon * epsilon_decay)

    env.close()
    history = {
        "success": np.array(successes, dtype=bool),
        "episode_return": np.array(episode_returns, dtype=float),
        "episode_length": np.array(episode_lengths, dtype=int),
        "epsilon": np.array(epsilons, dtype=float),
        "params": {
            "episodes": episodes,
            "max_steps_per_episode": max_steps_per_episode,
            "alpha": alpha,
            "gamma": gamma,
            "epsilon_start": epsilon_start,
            "epsilon_end": epsilon_end,
            "epsilon_decay": epsilon_decay,
            "map_name": map_name,
            "is_slippery": is_slippery,
            "seed": seed,
            "reward_mode": reward_mode,
            "step_penalty": step_penalty,
            "hole_penalty": hole_penalty,
            "goal_reward": goal_reward,
        },
    }
    return Q, history

Note: Reading the Policy Plot¶

  • H means hole, a terminal failure state.
  • G means goal, a terminal success state.
  • Arrows show the action with the highest Q-value in each non-terminal state.
  • Brighter squares mean larger maximum Q-values.

Use this plot to see whether the learned policy moves around holes and toward the goal.

Step 7. Animate the Learned Policy During Training¶

Sometimes a single final policy plot hides the learning process.

The next cells create an updating GIF that shows how the policy and state values change as training progresses.

Suggested uses:

  • keep the default settings and watch the policy become more organized
  • compare deterministic vs. slippery FrozenLake
  • change the snapshot interval to make the GIF shorter or smoother
In [ ]:
def policy_frame_array(Q, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, title="Policy snapshot"):
    """Render a policy plot to an RGB image array so it can be written into a GIF."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    grid = decode_grid(env)
    n_rows, n_cols = grid.shape

    values = np.max(Q, axis=1).reshape(n_rows, n_cols)

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 5))
    image = ax.imshow(values)
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(n_cols))
    ax.set_yticks(np.arange(n_rows))

    for state in range(Q.shape[0]):
        row, col = divmod(state, n_cols)
        tile = grid[row, col]

        if tile == "H":
            label = "H"
        elif tile == "G":
            label = "G"
        else:
            # Random tie-breaking is useful during training, but for a stable figure
            # we show the greedy action from np.argmax here.
            label = ACTION_ARROWS[int(np.argmax(Q[state]))]

        ax.text(col, row, label, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=18)

    cbar = fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax)
    cbar.set_label("max Q-value")
    plt.tight_layout()

    fig.canvas.draw()
    width, height = fig.canvas.get_width_height()
    frame = np.frombuffer(fig.canvas.buffer_rgba(), dtype=np.uint8).reshape(height, width, 4)[..., :3].copy()
    plt.close(fig)
    env.close()
    return frame


def train_q_learning_with_snapshots(
    episodes=3000,
    max_steps_per_episode=100,
    alpha=0.30,
    gamma=0.95,
    epsilon_start=1.00,
    epsilon_end=0.05,
    epsilon_decay=0.995,
    map_name=MAP_NAME,
    is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY,
    seed=SEED,
    reward_mode="default",
    step_penalty=0.0,
    hole_penalty=0.0,
    goal_reward=1.0,
    snapshot_interval=250
):
    """Train Q-learning and save policy snapshots every snapshot_interval episodes."""
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    n_states = env.observation_space.n
    n_actions = env.action_space.n

    Q = np.zeros((n_states, n_actions))
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)

    successes = []
    episode_returns = []
    episode_lengths = []
    epsilons = []

    snapshots = []
    epsilon = epsilon_start

    # Initial frame before training
    snapshots.append({
        "episode": 0,
        "Q": Q.copy()
    })

    for episode in range(episodes):
        state, info = env.reset(seed=seed + episode)
        original_return = 0.0
        reached_goal = False

        for step in range(max_steps_per_episode):
            if rng.random() < epsilon:
                action = int(rng.integers(n_actions))
            else:
                action = greedy_action(Q, state, rng)

            next_state, original_reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
            done = terminated or truncated

            learning_reward = apply_reward_mode(
                env,
                next_state,
                original_reward,
                reward_mode=reward_mode,
                step_penalty=step_penalty,
                hole_penalty=hole_penalty,
                goal_reward=goal_reward
            )

            best_next_q = np.max(Q[next_state])
            bootstrap = 0.0 if terminated else best_next_q
            td_target = learning_reward + gamma * bootstrap
            td_error = td_target - Q[state, action]
            Q[state, action] = Q[state, action] + alpha * td_error

            original_return += original_reward
            if original_reward > 0:
                reached_goal = True

            state = next_state
            if done:
                break

        successes.append(reached_goal)
        episode_returns.append(original_return)
        episode_lengths.append(step + 1)
        epsilons.append(epsilon)

        completed_episode = episode + 1
        if completed_episode % snapshot_interval == 0:
            snapshots.append({
                "episode": completed_episode,
                "Q": Q.copy()
            })

        epsilon = max(epsilon_end, epsilon * epsilon_decay)

    # Always include the final trained policy
    if snapshots[-1]["episode"] != episodes:
        snapshots.append({
            "episode": episodes,
            "Q": Q.copy()
        })

    env.close()

    history = {
        "success": np.array(successes, dtype=bool),
        "episode_return": np.array(episode_returns, dtype=float),
        "episode_length": np.array(episode_lengths, dtype=int),
        "epsilon": np.array(epsilons, dtype=float),
        "params": {
            "episodes": episodes,
            "max_steps_per_episode": max_steps_per_episode,
            "alpha": alpha,
            "gamma": gamma,
            "epsilon_start": epsilon_start,
            "epsilon_end": epsilon_end,
            "epsilon_decay": epsilon_decay,
            "map_name": map_name,
            "is_slippery": is_slippery,
            "seed": seed,
            "reward_mode": reward_mode,
            "step_penalty": step_penalty,
            "hole_penalty": hole_penalty,
            "goal_reward": goal_reward,
            "snapshot_interval": snapshot_interval
        }
    }

    return Q, history, snapshots


def save_policy_gif(snapshots, out_path, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, fps=2):
    """Convert saved Q-table snapshots into an animated GIF."""
    frames = []
    for snap in snapshots:
        title = f"Learned policy after episode {snap['episode']}"
        frame = policy_frame_array(
            snap["Q"],
            map_name=map_name,
            is_slippery=is_slippery,
            title=title
        )
        frames.append(frame)

    imageio.mimsave(out_path, frames, fps=fps, loop=0)
    return out_path

Step 8. Evaluate the Learned Greedy Policy¶

Now evaluate the fixed Q-table over multiple episodes.

During evaluation, the agent usually acts greedily, meaning it chooses the best action according to the learned Q-table instead of exploring.

The evaluation reports success rate, average return, and average episode length.

In [ ]:

def evaluate_agent(Q, episodes=100, max_steps_per_episode=100, epsilon=0.0, map_name=MAP_NAME, is_slippery=IS_SLIPPERY, seed=10_000):
    env = make_frozenlake(map_name=map_name, is_slippery=is_slippery)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    n_actions = env.action_space.n

    successes = []
    returns = []
    lengths = []

    for episode in range(episodes):
        state, info = env.reset(seed=seed + episode)
        total_reward = 0.0
        reached_goal = False

        for step in range(max_steps_per_episode):
            if rng.random() < epsilon:
                action = ...
            else:
                action = ...

            next_state, reward, terminated, truncated, info = ...
            done = terminated or truncated

            total_reward += reward
            if reward > 0:
                reached_goal = True
            state = next_state
            if done:
                break

        successes.append(reached_goal)
        returns.append(total_reward)
        lengths.append(step + 1)

    env.close()
    return {
        "success_rate": float(np.mean(successes)),
        "average_return": float(np.mean(returns)),
        "average_length": float(np.mean(lengths)),
    }

Step 10. Tinker Experiment Runner¶

The helper below runs one experiment using the baseline settings plus whichever overrides you provide.

Each experiment trains a new Q-table, prints the changed settings, plots the training curve, and plots the learned policy.

#   4. print the label and changed settings
#   5. plot training curve and policy
#   6. return Q_exp, history_exp

def run_tinker_experiment(label, **overrides):
    params = BASELINE_PARAMS.copy()
    params.update(overrides)

    Q_exp, history_exp = ...

    final_window = min(100, len(history_exp["success"]))
    final_success_rate = ...

    print("=" * 70)
    print(label)
    print("=" * 70)
    print(f"Final {final_window}-episode success rate: {final_success_rate:.1%}")
    print("Changed settings:")
    for key, value in overrides.items():
        print(f"  {key}: {value}")

    plot_training(history_exp, window=100, title=f"{label}: training success rate")
    plot_policy(
        Q_exp,
        map_name=params["map_name"],
        is_slippery=params["is_slippery"],
        title=f"{label}: learned policy",
    )

    return Q_exp, history_exp

Step 11. Group A: Learning Rate Experiment¶

The learning rate alpha controls how much each new update changes the Q-table.

Turn this group on to compare small, medium, and large learning rates. Watch for settings that learn too slowly or update too aggressively.

In [ ]:
RUN_GROUP_A = False  # Change to True if your group is testing learning rate.

if RUN_GROUP_A:
    for test_alpha in [0.00, 0.05, 0.30, 1.00]:
        run_tinker_experiment(
            label=f"Learning rate alpha = {test_alpha}",
            alpha=test_alpha
        )
else:
    print("Group A is off. Set RUN_GROUP_A = True to run this experiment.")

Step 12. Group B: Discount Factor Experiment¶

The discount factor gamma controls how much the agent values future rewards.

Turn this group on to compare agents that care mostly about immediate reward with agents that plan farther ahead.

In [ ]:
RUN_GROUP_B = False  # Change to True if your group is testing discount factor.

if RUN_GROUP_B:
    for test_gamma in [0.00, 0.50, 0.95, 0.99]:
        run_tinker_experiment(
            label=f"Discount factor gamma = {test_gamma}",
            gamma=test_gamma
        )
else:
    print("Group B is off. Set RUN_GROUP_B = True to run this experiment.")

Step 13. Group C: Exploration vs. Exploitation Experiment¶

Exploration controls how often the agent tries actions that are not currently estimated to be best.

Turn this group on to compare no exploration, small exploration, baseline exploration, and persistent exploration.

In [ ]:
RUN_GROUP_C = False  # Change to True if your group is testing exploration.

if RUN_GROUP_C:
    exploration_settings = [
        ("No exploration", {"epsilon_start": 0.00, "epsilon_end": 0.00, "epsilon_decay": 1.000}),
        ("Small exploration", {"epsilon_start": 0.20, "epsilon_end": 0.01, "epsilon_decay": 0.995}),
        ("Baseline exploration", {"epsilon_start": 1.00, "epsilon_end": 0.05, "epsilon_decay": 0.995}),
        ("Persistent exploration", {"epsilon_start": 1.00, "epsilon_end": 0.80, "epsilon_decay": 1.000}),
    ]

    for label, settings in exploration_settings:
        run_tinker_experiment(label=label, **settings)
else:
    print("Group C is off. Set RUN_GROUP_C = True to run this experiment.")

Step 14. Group D: Reward Shaping Experiment¶

Reward shaping changes the reward signal used for learning.

Turn this group on to compare default rewards, step penalties, hole penalties, and larger goal rewards. Look for how these choices change the learned policy and training curve.

In [ ]:
RUN_GROUP_D = False  # Change to True if your group is testing reward shaping.

if RUN_GROUP_D:
    reward_settings = [
        ("Default rewards", {
            "reward_mode": "default",
            "step_penalty": 0.0,
            "hole_penalty": 0.0,
            "goal_reward": 1.0
        }),
        ("Small step penalty", {
            "reward_mode": "custom",
            "step_penalty": -0.01,
            "hole_penalty": 0.0,
            "goal_reward": 1.0
        }),
        ("Hole penalty", {
            "reward_mode": "custom",
            "step_penalty": 0.0,
            "hole_penalty": -1.0,
            "goal_reward": 1.0
        }),
        ("Bigger goal reward plus step penalty", {
            "reward_mode": "custom",
            "step_penalty": -0.01,
            "hole_penalty": -1.0,
            "goal_reward": 5.0
        }),
    ]

    for label, settings in reward_settings:
        run_tinker_experiment(label=label, **settings)
else:
    print("Group D is off. Set RUN_GROUP_D = True to run this experiment.")

Step 15. Optional Challenge: Slippery FrozenLake¶

The slippery version has stochastic transitions, so actions do not always move the agent exactly as intended.

Turn this challenge on to see how Q-learning behaves when the environment is less predictable. Compare the policy and success rate to the deterministic baseline.

In [ ]:
RUN_SLIPPERY_CHALLENGE = False

if RUN_SLIPPERY_CHALLENGE:
    Q_slippery, history_slippery = run_tinker_experiment(
        label="Slippery FrozenLake baseline",
        is_slippery=True,
        episodes=8000,
        alpha=0.10,
        gamma=0.99,
        epsilon_start=1.00,
        epsilon_end=0.05,
        epsilon_decay=0.999
    )

    slippery_evaluation = evaluate_agent(
        Q_slippery,
        episodes=200,
        is_slippery=True
    )

    print("Slippery evaluation:")
    for key, value in slippery_evaluation.items():
        print(f"  {key}: {value:.3f}")
else:
    print("Slippery challenge is off. Set RUN_SLIPPERY_CHALLENGE = True to run it.")
